lens: iOS task completion, touch and accessibility layout, state semantics, backend parity, and failure recovery

findings.observation: The isolated iPhone 17 Simulator run passed 13 unit tests and 12 UI tests, including localhost fixture fetches, but no current VoiceOver traversal proves spoken labels, order, values, and state changes.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/round-2/final/command-results.json records the unit and UI xcresult summaries and the two successful localhost fixture requests; docs/evaluations/overnight/final/ios-review-sequence.json contains the prior AX5 dark-mode surface sequence.
findings.user_impact: Touch and large-text paths have direct evidence while a VoiceOver user may still encounter an unlabeled or confusing confirmation and outcome sequence.
findings.recommendation: Record a VoiceOver traversal of source evidence, each fact decision, action preview, and local outcome against the same frozen fixture.
findings.verification: VoiceOver announces identity, provenance, proposed versus confirmed state, exact target and effect, no-external-change result, and retry in logical order without duplicate or ambiguous controls.

strengths: The iOS project passed 13 unit tests and 12 UI tests in separate DerivedData directories with zero failures or skips.
The UI run fetched the frozen localhost fixture twice from 127.0.0.1:8787 and exercised the same synthetic evidence boundary.
A separate Release simulator build completed successfully with code signing disabled.
Prior direct AX5, dark-mode, ambiguity, no-action, prohibited-scoring, offline, and recovery evidence remains tied to the unchanged iOS implementation.
missing_evidence: A current VoiceOver spoken-order and control-state transcript.
open_questions: Does the same decision order remain efficient on the smallest supported iPhone rather than only the iPhone 17 simulator?
